name: Ad creatives (static, carousel and video concepts)
asked_as: our ads are tired, we need fresh ones
carousel ads for the new collection
outcome: A set of finished, on-brand ads the owner can upload today: image files in feed and Stories sizes plus their copy, each ad naming the buyer it is for, the gap it fills and the proof it shows, varied by idea rather than by colour, with one line per ad on where it goes and what will say it worked.
first_principles: On Meta today the creative is the targeting. Broad delivery finds people from what the ad says and shows, so a segment the data underfunds needs its own concepts (its occasion, its product, its words and picture), not the same ad with its name in the headline.

A concept is buyer x angle x offer, with format as a fourth axis. A new background, pose or colour is not a new ad: Meta groups near-copies as one and serves them to the same people. Ten ads that share three ideas are three ads.

Proven winners are the control. Relaunching or extending a winner is the cheapest new money; a new concept earns its place by beating the control on store-side cost per purchase, read after about 3 times the target cost per purchase has been spent on it. So the batch size comes from the test budget, not from a round number.

A format is chosen for the hypothesis, not for variety's sake: a review card for a trust gap, a comparison for a 'why pay more' doubt, a notes list or chat for cold native reach, an offer card only for buyers who already know the product. Real range comes from different gaps, each in the structure that answers it.

Fatigue is a reading, not a feeling: frequency up while click-through and return on ad spend fall on the same ad over the same weeks, with the account's cost per thousand flat. The fix is a refresh that changes one part (hook, person, setting, buyer framing) and keeps the idea that sold.

The ad sells a physical thing the buyer will hold. Use the real product photo and set every word in the brand's own fonts. An image model may make a scene or background with no words in it; it never draws the product, the logo, a price or a letter. A wrong detail in an ad comes back as a return.

questions.ask: Is this for one product, your bestsellers, or the range as a whole?
questions.why: It decides which photos, proof and buyers the set is built on, and whether each ad sells one item or sends people to a collection.

options.label: Bestsellers
options.pro: proven demand, the fastest read on new ideas
options.con: can speed up fatigue on what already runs

options.label: One product
options.pro: depth: its own concept per buyer and objection
options.con: slow to read if it is not yet a proven seller

options.label: The range or the brand
options.pro: reaches buyers who want choice
options.con: hardest to sell in one image; needs carousels and a collection page that converts

questions.default: The two or three products with the most store gross profit in the last 90 days

questions.settle_with_data: Rank products by store revenue and gross profit over 90 days and set that next to ad spend by product. Products with high gross profit and little spend are named as the underfed candidates; say the ranking and its source in one line instead of asking.

questions.ask: Do these need to carry a sale, a launch or a festival, or are they evergreen?
questions.why: An offer or a date changes the formats allowed (offer card, countdown), the copy, the end date on the image and how long the ads can run.

options.label: Evergreen
options.pro: can run for months; no end date on the image
options.con: no urgency to lean on

options.label: A sale or offer
options.pro: the strongest pull for buyers who already know you
options.con: trains buyers to wait; needs a live offer and its break-even worked out

options.label: A festival or season
options.pro: a moment buyers already plan for (gifting, weddings, weather)
options.con: short life; must be live before buyers start shopping

questions.default: Evergreen, with one moment piece for any region or season the data names
skip_if: the brief names an offer, launch or festival
questions.settle_with_data: Check the store's live offers, the next 6 weeks of the calendar against last year's sales by week, and any region or season that stands out in the segment table.

questions.ask: Static images only, or carousels and video concepts too?
questions.why: Each needs different material: statics need photos, carousels need 3 to 7 cards of story or range, video needs footage or a person who can film.

options.label: Statics only
options.pro: fast, cheap, every word exact
options.con: misses buyers who mostly watch Reels

options.label: Statics plus carousels
options.pro: carousels show range, steps or several proofs
options.con: more cards to make and check

options.label: Statics plus video concepts
options.pro: covers Reels and Stories where much spend goes
options.con: video needs a script and a shoot; handed to the video-scripts journey

questions.default: Statics, plus a carousel where the gap is range or steps
questions.settle_with_data: Read spend and store-side cost per purchase by format (image, video, carousel) and by placement. If video holds most spend at a better cost, include video concepts; if an existing format has never been tried, say so.

questions.ask: How many ads should I make?
questions.why: More concepts than the test budget can read is noise: each one needs spend to get a verdict.

options.label: The number you asked for
options.pro: what you planned
options.con: may be more than the budget can read

options.label: What the budget can read
options.pro: every ad gets a fair verdict
options.con: may be fewer than you hoped

questions.default: The brief's number; if none, the monthly test budget divided by about 3 times the target cost per purchase
questions.settle_with_data: Work it out from the test budget and the target cost per purchase (from gross profit per purchase). If the asked number is far above what the budget can read, make it anyway and say in one line how many to launch first.

look_for: Underfunded segments: revenue share well above spend share, on 15 or more purchases, often an older age band, a region, or men buying gifts. Each one gets its own concepts in its own words and occasion.
Concentration: one or two ads holding most of the spend. Normal under campaign budgets, but when they tire the account tires with them, so their successors must be built before they fall.

Fatigue on the same ad: frequency rising, click-through and return on ad spend falling for two or more weeks, with the account's cost per thousand flat. If cost per thousand rose across the whole account, it is the auction, not the ad.
A lookalike set: live ads that differ only in colour, crop or headline. Count concepts, not ads; 30 ads on 5 ideas means the gap is ideas, not volume.

False winners: high click-through with few purchases (a curiosity hook pulling the wrong people), or high return on ad spend that comes from existing customers and retargeting. Judge on new-customer cost per purchase against store orders.
Awareness skew: nearly every ad speaks to people who already know the product (product shots, offers). Cold reach needs problem- and desire-led ads; most-aware ads belong in a small share.
Proof left unused: a review theme, a guarantee, a measured spec or a true founder story that buyers name but no ad shows.
Objections no ad answers: the top return reason or pre-purchase question (size, quality in person, delivery time, COD, is it real) answered by nothing in the account.
Paused winners: old ads with good store-side cost per purchase switched off with no reason recorded. The cheapest new ad is a relaunch.
Moments missing: a region or season that stands out in the data with no ad that names its occasion.
A page leak: ads earn clicks but the landing page converts well below the store's own average. New ads will not fix that; say so in one line and point to the product-pages journey.
Rivals' long runners: ads live for months show what the category rewards. Take the structure; never the words or the art.

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: most live concepts are product shots or offers; cold new-customer cost rising
hypothesis_patterns.bet: problem- and desire-led ads in native formats (notes list, chat, problem scene) for cold buyers

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: a review, return or chat theme above about 10% with no ad that answers it
hypothesis_patterns.bet: one objection-answer ad per objection, each with its own real proof

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: strong photo reviews, a guarantee or a founder story that no ad shows
hypothesis_patterns.bet: review card, review wall or founder note built from it

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: a region or season with revenue share above its spend share, or a dated occasion in the next 6 weeks
hypothesis_patterns.bet: a moment ad those buyers know, live before they start shopping

hypothesis_patterns.evidence: rival ads running for months, review themes, the product page
hypothesis_patterns.bet: 3 concepts on the category's proven structures, each read at about 3 times target cost per purchase

decisions.ask: How different should these be from what runs now?

options.label: Like your winners: their format with new angles, plus one nearby format
options.pro: safest and fastest to read; reuses an idea that sold
options.con: the same buyers see the same idea, so fatigue comes sooner
options.when: winners are still fresh (frequency low) and the test budget is small

options.label: A mix: one control in your winner's format, the rest new concepts in new formats (my usual pick)
options.pro: keeps sales steady while the account learns
options.con: fewer brand-new ideas in this batch
options.when: winners exist and at least one is tiring, or one ad holds most of the spend

options.label: Mostly new formats and concepts, still with one control
options.pro: the most to learn; opens new buyers
options.con: more misses, more budget to read, slower
options.when: no judged winners, winners fully worn out, or a new buyer or product to open

decisions.recommend: From the diagnosis: a tiring winner or heavy concentration means the mix; no ad with enough purchases to judge means mostly new, on the category's proven structures; fresh winners and a small budget means like your winners. Every option keeps one control so the read is fair. Which buyers get the rows comes from brand-brain.mjs plan: most to proven segments, a share to underfunded winners, about 15% to tests.

decisions.ask: One format you like, or shall I match a format to each gap?

options.label: Your chosen format
options.pro: the look you want, consistent across the set
options.con: one format reads as one ad to Meta, and if it does not fit the gap the whole set misses
options.when: a format has clearly won for this store and you want more of it: then each new ad is a new concept inside it

options.label: I match a format to each gap (my usual pick)
options.pro: each ad uses the structure that answers its gap; at least 4 layouts and 3 native formats in a set of 10
options.con: a less uniform look across the set

options.label: Try many formats to learn
options.pro: finds which formats work for this store
options.con: each format gets thin budget, so results are hard to read
options.when: a new account with no format history and enough budget for each

decisions.recommend: Match a format to each gap, unless data/creatives.md shows one format clearly winning: then keep it for the control and spread the new concepts over the formats their gaps call for.

rules: Every ad has a plan row: segment, the number behind it, persona, insight in their words, angle, format, proof with its source, hook. A row with no insight is cut, never filled with a guess.
Real product photos only. An image model makes a background or scene with no words in it; the product, logo, price and every letter are set on top in HTML in the brand's fonts, then rendered.
'10 more' of a format means 10 new concepts inside that format (a new buyer, objection, moment or proof), pulled fresh from the format's skill, never the same layout reworded.

Pick formats from formats.json by insight_fit: name the gap first, then a format whose fit includes it and whose needs the store meets (no real reviews, no review card; no founder, no founder note; never a faked chat, review, press mention or countdown).

A set of 10 or more uses at least 4 distinct layouts, none on more than 30% of the set, at least 3 native formats (notes list, chat, comparison table, review card, explainer), and a button on at least 70% of the ads.

The product fills at least a third of the frame and is the item the copy names; no watermark, logo or text from the source photo survives the crop; a review quote sits only on the product it is about.
Hooks start from customer words or a proven ad line, at the brand's sentence length and reading level.
Words, logo, price and the product's key detail sit inside the safe zones: feed 4:5, and 9:16 with about 14% of the top, 35% of the bottom and 6% of each side kept clear.
The button copies the brand's own button in its real ads (shape, colour, words), drawn on the image with a tight box in the manifest.
Prices match the live page today and are written the Indian way (₹1,00,000). Stock and time limits only when real. Offer cards only with a live offer whose break-even is worked out.
Absolute claims (every, all, 100%, guaranteed, the only) must be true across the whole range, or softened.
Never an AI-made person shown as a customer, reviewer or founder.
Run copy-check on every headline and line with context/never-say.txt in place; a banned claim covers its meaning ('all natural' also rules out 'every stone is natural').

Each size is its own layout: Stories and Reels (9:16) are designed for the tall frame, with the product larger and every word inside the safe zone (about 14% top and 35% bottom clear). Never the feed card placed on a blurred or plain band.
Build every creative from an HTML or SVG source and run copy-check and the consistency check on the source folder, so banned words and unsourced offers are caught before rendering.

checks: Every line of copy and on-image text through check-ad-copy-for-policy-and-claims (Meta rules, ASCI in India, personal attributes, 'free', comparisons).
Every frame with an AI-made part through keep-product-accurate-in-ai-media: label, colour, shape and size match the real product.
Each finished ad through prelaunch-ad-check before it is called ready.
senior_review: Would a stranger in the target segment know in one second what this is, who it is for and why now?
Can I point each ad to its gap and the number or quote behind it?
Are these 10 concepts, or 3 concepts in 10 colours? Would Meta group any two as one?
Is the current best winner in the plan as the control, so the new ones have something to beat?
Is there anything the owner cannot stand behind: a claim, a price, a stock line, a person?
Does the page each ad points to keep the ad's promise on the first phone screen?
Could the owner upload this today without asking me a single question?

How many new concepts can this test budget read, and after how much spend?
What share of cold ads should speak to buyers who do not know the product yet?
Which static formats answer a trust objection, and which a price objection?
What makes a hook filter for buyers rather than just stop the scroll?
What counts as a new concept rather than a variation under Andromeda?
Meta sizes and safe zones for feed, Stories and Reels images
Indian rules (ASCI) on comparison ads, 'free', limited-stock claims and drip pricing
Meta rules on implying a viewer's personal attributes

never: Brand voice, product facts, prices and customer quotes come from the org context and the store, never from the library.
Card ids stay in the trace, never on an ad or in the hand-over.

files: PNG files at 1080 x 1350 (feed) and 1080 x 1920 (Stories and Reels), one folder per concept, with their HTML sources
copy.md: primary text, headline, description and button per ad, plus language versions if asked
manifest.json beside the images: layout, format, product, segment, moment, button box and the source of any absolute claim
A short hand-over: per ad, one line on the gap it fills and its evidence, where it goes (its own test ad set inside the proven campaign) and the number that will say it worked
A bulk-upload sheet for paused ads, when asked
next_moves: 10 more in the format that wins this batch, as new concepts
The landing page these ads should point to, with the same promise (product-pages journey)
Video scripts for the two strongest concepts (video-scripts journey)
A launch sheet that adds these to the live campaign without knocking winners back into learning
